body:
`TIER1_PATHS_REGEX` (`\.(po|pot|md)$|^README`) has been in
`.github/policy/tier-policy.config` and on the `Policy` dataclass since the module was
written. It was parsed, exposed in `describe`, and **consulted nowhere**. `validate_fork_pr`
never referenced it, so a PR labelled `safe-tier-1` was path-checked only against
`FORBIDDEN_PATHS_REGEX` (auth/csrf/session/admin/migrations/deps/container) -- leaving the
whole of `cps/` outside those areas eligible to auto-merge with no human eyes.

Measured before the fix, with negative controls to show the validator could still refuse:

    validate-fork-pr --tier safe-tier-1  files=[cps/opds.py]      -> {"ok": true}
    validate-fork-pr --tier safe-tier-1  files=[requirements.txt] -> forbidden_path
    validate-fork-pr --tier safe-tier-1  base=some-feature-branch -> unprotected_base

Nothing else covered it, and each near-miss is worth naming because each looks like it does:

- `tier-label-guard.yml` restricts **who** may apply the label, never **what** the PR touches.
- `auto-merge.yml`'s CHANGES-vs-upstream requirement runs only `if [ "$tier" = "safe-tier-2" ]`,
  and its own comment states the reason: *"Tier-1 (.po + *.md only) is exempt."* That premise
  was never established anywhere -- the exemption rests on the unchecked property.
- The tier table in CLAUDE.md defines tier-1 as ".po / *.md / README, no code", so the rule was
  documented policy carried entirely by whoever applied the label.

Real instance: **#1529**, an auto-revert opened by our own automation, sat labelled
`safe-tier-1` while reverting `cps/opds.py` and deleting `test_1097_opds_discover_naming.py`
(194 lines). Simulated against `main` it merged CLEAN and left the CHANGELOG entry claiming
the fix had shipped -- code reverted, regression test gone, release notes still advertising it.
Closed by hand on 2026-08-12 rather than merged.

Fixed by enforcing the allowlist in `validate_fork_pr` for `safe-tier-1`, failing closed with a
new `tier1_paths` category that names the offending files. Red/green: two new tests fail
without the change, 25 pass with it; tier-2 is deliberately unaffected.

Follow-up worth a deliberate decision rather than a silent widening: `findings/items/*.json`
is not on the allowlist, so ledger-only PRs (#1487, and #1534 which I merged as tier-1 myself)
now demote to needs-review. That may be the right call or the allowlist may want extending --
but extending it is a config edit, which is precisely the deliberation the gate exists to force.
title: safe-tier-1's path allowlist was loaded but never enforced
